blocks.heading: Locating at home or abroad
blocks.text: An overseas location may offer access to customers, inputs, skills or lower specified operating costs. It can also create transport, communication, currency, coordination and unfamiliar-market risks. A home location can preserve known suppliers, management access and customer understanding while sometimes limiting reach. Compare verified total relevant costs and service reliability; neither a foreign nor a home label establishes the better option. Separate one-time relocation costs from ongoing costs and check whether potential incentives are actually available rather than treating them as guaranteed.
blocks.reviewed_unchanged: Re-read the location comparison after making its case dependence explicit; the costs, service requirements and conditional recommendation remain valid.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nara Goods compares remaining near its established Namibian customers with a foreign site that has cheaper stated rent but longer delivery and coordination demands. The rent saving is one benefit, not the whole decision. Lost responsiveness and extra delivery costs may outweigh it, especially for urgent customised orders.
